subject: psychology
promptStrong: Give me a challenging GCSE exam-style question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the Edexcel spec.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for GCSE Edexcel Psychology simply, with an example and the most common mistake.

questions.q: The Edexcel spec requires symptoms of depression and addiction to be learned according to which classification system?
questions.explain: Edexcel requires symptoms and features of unipolar depression and addiction to be learned according to the International Classification of Diseases (ICD).

questions.q: Which of these is a core symptom of unipolar depression?
questions.explain: A persistent lowering of mood is a core symptom of unipolar depression, along with low energy and loss of interest or motivation.

questions.q: What is 'withdrawal' in the context of addiction?
options: The first time a substance is used
Choosing to stop using with no effects
A set of unpleasant physical and psychological symptoms when trying to stop
questions.explain: Withdrawal is the set of unpleasant physical and psychological symptoms a person experiences when trying to stop or cut down an addiction.

questions.q: Which factor could help explain why the recorded incidence of depression appears to change over time?
options: The gene for depression changing each year
Changes in diagnosis, awareness and reduced stigma
questions.explain: Recorded incidence changes over time partly because of changes in diagnostic criteria, greater awareness and reduced stigma, not just true prevalence.

questions.q: The Edexcel spec says mental health problems affect the individual in which three ways?
questions.explain: The specification requires the impact on the individual to be considered in social, emotional and occupational terms.

questions.q: Which of these is an example of the impact of mental health problems on society rather than on the individual?
questions.explain: Societal impacts include healthcare demand, crime and economic costs; the other options describe effects on the individual.

questions.q: Which research method is most useful for investigating the influence of genes on depression and addiction?
questions.explain: Family, twin and adoption studies allow researchers to compare concordance rates and estimate the genetic contribution to depression and addiction.

questions.q: A student says depression is caused entirely by genes. Why is this a weakness of a purely genetic explanation?
options: Genes have no role at all in depression
It ignores the role of the environment and stressful life events
questions.explain: A purely genetic explanation is reductionist because it ignores environmental factors such as stressful life events, which interact with genes.

questions.q: Beck's cognitive theory of depression describes negative views of which three things (the cognitive triad)?
options: The self, the world and the future
The past, the present and other people
questions.explain: Beck's cognitive triad is negative and irrational thinking about the self, the world and the future.

questions.q: A person with depression thinks 'I always fail and I always will'. Which cognitive concept does this show?
questions.explain: This overgeneralised, negative and unrealistic belief is a cognitive error (faulty thinking), central to the cognitive explanation of depression.

questions.q: A person feels calmer after a cigarette, so keeps smoking to gain that reward. Which learning process explains this?
questions.explain: Repeating a behaviour because it produces a rewarding outcome is positive reinforcement, an operant conditioning explanation of addiction.

questions.q: A teenager starts gambling after watching an admired older sibling gamble. Which learning explanation fits best?
options: Social learning by observation and imitation
questions.explain: Copying the behaviour of an admired role model is social learning theory: learning by observation and imitation, possibly with vicarious reinforcement.

questions.q: What is the central premise of cognitive behavioural therapy (CBT)?
options: Drugs must be used before therapy
Thoughts determine feelings, so faulty thoughts can be changed
Behaviour is caused only by genes
questions.explain: CBT is based on the premise that thoughts determine feelings, so patients learn to monitor and change faulty, irrational thoughts and behaviours.

questions.q: Which is a strength of using CBT rather than drugs to treat depression?
options: It gives the patient coping skills to help prevent relapse
It removes the need for the patient to engage
It works instantly with no effort
questions.explain: CBT teaches long-term coping skills and relapse prevention by changing thinking patterns, rather than only managing symptoms like drugs do.

questions.q: Anti-depressant drugs such as SSRIs are used to treat depression by acting on which neurotransmitter system?
questions.explain: SSRIs (selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors) increase the availability of serotonin, targeting the serotonin system linked to depression.

questions.q: Which of these is a common weakness of using drug treatments for depression or addiction?
options: They can cause side effects and may not work once stopped
questions.explain: Drug treatments can have side effects and often treat symptoms rather than causes, so problems may return once the drugs are stopped.

questions.q: Caspi et al. (2003) investigated the interaction between stressful life events and which gene in predicting depression?
questions.explain: Caspi et al. studied a polymorphism in the 5-HTT (serotonin transporter) gene and its moderation of life stress in predicting depression.

questions.q: Caspi et al. (2003) found that people carrying a short (s) allele of the 5-HTT gene were more likely to become depressed after stressful life events. This best supports which model?
questions.explain: The finding that a genetic vulnerability only led to depression when combined with stress supports the diathesis-stress model of gene x environment interaction.

questions.q: Young (2007) investigated the effectiveness of CBT as a treatment for which problem?
questions.explain: Young (2007) studied the outcomes of cognitive behaviour therapy with internet addicts, finding CBT helped reduce compulsive internet use.

questions.q: Which pairing correctly matches an explanation to the nature-nurture debate?
options: Learning theory = nature; drug treatment = nurture
Genetic explanation = nature; learning theory = nurture
questions.explain: Genetic explanations and drug treatments sit on the nature side, while cognitive theory, learning theory and CBT sit on the nurture side of the debate.
